A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, Figures 1–2, and Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching across the revised page layout.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report original synthetic experiments on misspecified three-class logistic regression, with classifier-direction errors and error bars from 100 trials.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original logistic-regression simulation and adds results with a fixed total label budget in Figure 2(ii). These are original simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: The ranking aggregation procedure, generalized majority vote, logistic-regression loss, and nearest-neighbor aggregation in Appendix C are unchanged. The added experiment uses the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 5 retains the truncated-quadratic illustration and the synthetic misspecified logistic task with d=2 and k=3. The added panel uses the same data-generating model; changing sample allocation does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain non-aggregated versus majority-vote behavior and the same aggregation levels, including m=1. No comparison method is added, removed, or replaced in the new panel.

E3.justification: Figure 2 adds an experiment with n=640,000/m, holding nm fixed across m in {1,4,16,64,256,1024}. The original n=10,000 experiment remains as panel (i). This is an additional budget control, with the task, model parameters, and error metric retained.

E4.justification: The new Figure 2(ii) tests whether the benefit of increasing aggregation persists when the total number of labels is held constant. This supplements the existing aggregation-level analysis with a resource-budget control.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 trials and 95% error bars for the logistic simulation. V3 extends the same reporting practice to the added panel and corrects the caption's 'each n' to 'each m'; no different run count or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 2(ii) adds results showing decreasing classifier-direction error as m increases under the fixed 640,000-label budget. Figure 1 and the original Figure 2 curve are retained unchanged. The added results use different sample sizes and are not same-setting performance improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects the absolute-continuity step from requiring ν(C)≤δ to requiring μ(C)≤δ. Lemma B.1 changes β=α/(α−1) to β=α/(1−α), agreeing with the existing derivation and main text. These are localized mathematical corrections, with the main theoretical results retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and closing discussion retain the same central claims: aggregation can strengthen surrogate consistency and recover consistency under model misspecification where unaggregated approaches fail. The new simulation supports these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: V3 explains the response-space expansion behind the ranking example, clarifies that identifying surrogates need not use argmax decoding, and suggests sharper aggregation bounds for nearly consistent surrogates. Existing limitations concerning asymptotic aggregation and optimal predictability remain.

D1.justification: The expanded Figure 2 caption documents the sample-allocation rule n=640,000/m for reproducing the added experiment. The existing corrupted-link parameters and fixed-n setup remain, with no additional optimizer, hardware, or code-access information.

R1.justification: The same 52 referenced works and substantive positioning relative to surrogate-consistency and H-consistency research are retained. Added author-name citations, revised Zhang reference pointers, and bibliographic formatting changes do not introduce new literature or redefine the research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds several short explanations, a footnote clarifying the use of k, and local wording and citation edits. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact; there is no extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from one large plot to two smaller side-by-side panels, with panel labels and an expanded caption. Caption styling, title formatting, and page flow also change locally, while the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Figure 2(ii) adds evidence that the declining-error trend persists when annotation cost is controlled, complementing v2's fixed-n simulation. The corrections in Appendix B.1 and Lemma B.1 remove local mathematical errors, and the explanatory additions improve clarity. These are useful but limited gains; the central theory, experimental scope, and stated asymptotic limitations remain largely unchanged.
